title: Concession and Mood in Bioethical Argument

sections.content: You know *a pesar de*, *a pesar de que* and *pese a* from B1 Unit 32. At C1, bioethical essays use *a pesar de que* and the more formal *pese a que* with a deliberate mood contrast. The indicative concedes an established clinical fact that the writer treats as known and relevant (*A pesar de que el fármaco demostró eficacia, causó efectos secundarios*). The subjunctive marks a hypothetical, future or backgrounded objection that the writer does not treat as decisive (*Pese a que existan dudas sobre el costo, la terapia génica avanza*). To compress a conceded completed action with the same subject, formal prose uses *pese a haber* + past participle.

sections.title: Concessive structures in formal argument
rows: *a pesar de que / pese a que* + indicative
Established fact (*A pesar de que el placebo produjo alivio, no sustituye al tratamiento.*)
*a pesar de que / pese a que* + subjunctive
Hypothetical, future or backgrounded objection (*Pese a que surjan efectos secundarios leves, el ensayo continúa.*)
Concise formal concession (*Pese a los riesgos, la investigación biomédica es necesaria.*)
Same subject, conceded completed action (*Pese a haber mejorado la prevención, el hospital necesita más recursos.*)

items.spanish: A pesar de que el fármaco mostró una alta eficacia, algunos participantes sufrieron efectos secundarios.
items.english: Although the drug showed high efficacy, some participants suffered side effects.

items.spanish: Pese a que existan reparos éticos sobre la terapia génica, el debate científico sigue abierto.
items.english: Even though ethical objections to gene therapy may exist, the scientific debate remains open.

items.spanish: Pese a haber superado las pruebas frente al placebo, el tratamiento requiere seguimiento prolongado.
items.english: Despite having passed the tests against the placebo, the treatment requires extended monitoring.

items.spanish: A pesar de los avances en la prevención, la investigación biomédica sigue enfrentando dilemas complejos.
items.english: Despite advances in prevention, biomedical research continues to face complex dilemmas.

sections.content: Never drop *que* before a conjugated verb (*pese a el fármaco funciona* is wrong: write *pese a que el fármaco funciona*) and never add *que* before a noun or infinitive (*a pesar de que los riesgos* is wrong: write *a pesar de los riesgos*).
